title: Mission Zero — Orientation & First Alert
disclaimer: All hosts, IPs, hashes, and personnel are fabricated for defensive training. No real systems are involved.

briefing.context: You are a CyberLabs analyst on shift for the MOD-HEAVY training floor. Northglass Logistics is a simulated client network used only for defensive drills.
roe: Defend only — investigate, contain, escalate, document.
Never attempt to exploit, reverse-engineer for flags, or attack any system.
Treat all evidence as simulated fiction.
When unsure, isolate and escalate rather than dig deeper into risky curiosity.
briefing.objective: Classify the inbound alert severity and choose a safe first action. Score is based on judgment, not speed-runs.

alert.summary: Unusual outbound connection pattern after a scheduled software update window. Sensor flagged repeated short bursts to an unfamiliar external IP in documentation range 203.0.113.0/24 (TEST-NET-3).
noise: Nightly inventory sync ran on schedule 20 minutes earlier (expected).
Same host had a false-positive adware alert last month (closed, benign).

severity.prompt: How would you classify this alert for Northglass Logistics?

options.label: Informational
options.feedback: Too soft. Repeated unknown egress after an update window deserves more than a shrug — even if it turns out benign.

options.label: Low
options.feedback: Defensible as a first pass, but the unknown destination and burst pattern suggest you should treat it as at least medium until cleared.

options.label: Medium
options.feedback: Solid call. Unknown egress + post-update timing warrants active triage without panicking the floor.

options.label: Critical
options.feedback: Possible over-escalation. Volume is small and there's no confirmed data loss yet — medium keeps urgency without burning the pager for every anomalous blip.

options.label: Investigate logs
options.detail: Pull EDR timeline, DNS, and proxy summaries for NG-WRKSTN-042 (read-only).
options.feedback: Good first move. Understanding scope before you touch the host keeps you from flying blind — and stays defensive.

options.label: Isolate host
options.detail: Network-quarantine NG-WRKSTN-042 via EDR containment policy.
options.feedback: Safe containment. Isolation stops further egress; follow up with log review so you know what you locked down.

options.label: Escalate to shift lead
options.detail: Hand off to Sam with alert ID NGL-SOC-8841 and your severity call.
options.feedback: Reasonable when you're unsure. Escalation is a strength — just capture what you've already observed so Sam isn't starting cold.

options.label: Ignore / close as noise
options.detail: Mark false positive based on last month's adware ticket.
options.feedback: Unsafe. Prior false positives don't clear a new unknown egress pattern. Closing early is how small problems become incidents.

loreUnlock.title: Ops Floor Memo — Fragment
loreUnlock.body:
FROM: Training Division archive
SUBJECT: Why we call it MOD-HEAVY

"Heavy" isn't about firepower. It's about the weight of the decision when the floor is quiet and the alert isn't. Contain first. Curiosity later — and never past the ROE.

— Sam
(SIMULATED training lore)

scoreBands.label: Sharp judgment
scoreBands.note: You balanced urgency with process. Ready for deeper modules when they ship.

scoreBands.label: Solid trainee
scoreBands.note: Core instincts are sound. Re-read the ROE and evidence noise next time.

scoreBands.label: Needs a second pass
scoreBands.note: Re-run Mission Zero with the briefing open. Prefer investigate / isolate / escalate over closing early.
